chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the most supportive of manners upon the religion is asceticism (zuhd) in the world.'

key_terms.الزُّهْدَ: Asceticism or detachment from worldly desires

ai.seo_question: What is the most supportive moral trait for religion according to Amir al-Mu'minin?
ai.summary: In this chain from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) transmits from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) that zuhd (asceticism) is not merely renunciation but a critical moral pillar that fortifies the practice of religion against worldly distractions. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with worldly engagement, where zuhd serves as the mechanism to preserve religious integrity. It highlights the practical implication that detachment from material excess is essential for sustaining faith in a transient world.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the most supportive of manners upon the world is the ascetism in the world’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from abu Hamza from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib) (a.s.) has said, ‘The most supportive, of religious moral behavior, is abstinence from worldly matters.’”
